items.readable_text:
Content:
We can use the standard algorithm when we want to multiply a three-digit number by a two-digit number.

Content:
As an example, let's find [MATH: 706 \times 25.] As always, we write the problem down in the following way:

Content:
[MATH: 7|0|6; ×|0|0|0|2|5|3, 530 + 14, 120 = 17, 650]

Content:
First, we multiply the top number ([MATH: 706]) by the ones digit of the second ([MATH: \bbox[2px, lightgray]{5}]).

Content:
[MATH: [math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]|[math]\color{blue}3[/math]; 7|0|6; ×|0|0|0|2|5; 3|5|3|0|706 × 5 = 3, 530000000,]

Content:
Next, we multiply top number ([MATH: 706]) by [MATH: \bbox[2px, lightgray]{2}0.] Let's do this in steps:

Content:
Step 1: We add a zero underneath the result of the first calculation, in the ones place:

Content:
[MATH: [math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]|[math]\color{blue}3[/math]; 7|0|6; ×|0|0|0|2|5; 3|5|3|0; 1|4|1|2|0|706 × 20 = 14, 1200000,]

Content:
Step 2: We continue to work out [MATH: 706\times \bbox[2px, lightgray]{2}0,] proceeding as usual:

Content:
[MATH: [math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]; [math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]|[math]\color{blue}1[/math]; [math]\color{blue}3[/math]; 7|0|6; ×|0|0|0|2|5; 3|5|3|0; 1|4|1|2|0|706 × 20 = 14, 1200000,]

Content:
Finally, we add the results:

Content:
[MATH: [math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]; [math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]|[math]\color{blue}1[/math]; [math]\color{blue}3[/math]; 7|0|6; ×|0|0|0|2|5; 3|5|3|0; +|1|4|1|2|0; 1|7|6|5|0|3, 530 + 14, 120 = 17, 650]

Content:
Therefore, [MATH: 706 \times 25 = 17 , 650.]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
We can use the standard algorithm when we want to multiply a three-digit number by a two-digit number.

Content:
As an example, let's find [MATH: 706 \times 25.] As always, we write the problem down in the following way:

Content:
[MATH: 7|0|6; ×|0|0|0|2|5|3, 530 + 14, 120 = 17, 650]

Content:
First, we multiply the top number ([MATH: 706]) by the ones digit of the second ([MATH: \bbox[2px, lightgray]{5}]).

Content:
[MATH: [math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]|[math]\color{blue}3[/math]; 7|0|6; ×|0|0|0|2|5; 3|5|3|0|706 × 5 = 3, 530000000,]

Content:
Next, we multiply top number ([MATH: 706]) by [MATH: \bbox[2px, lightgray]{2}0.] Let's do this in steps:

Content:
Step 1: We add a zero underneath the result of the first calculation, in the ones place:

Content:
[MATH: [math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]|[math]\color{blue}3[/math]; 7|0|6; ×|0|0|0|2|5; 3|5|3|0; 1|4|1|2|0|706 × 20 = 14, 1200000,]

Content:
Step 2: We continue to work out [MATH: 706\times \bbox[2px, lightgray]{2}0,] proceeding as usual:

Content:
[MATH: [math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]; [math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]|[math]\color{blue}1[/math]; [math]\color{blue}3[/math]; 7|0|6; ×|0|0|0|2|5; 3|5|3|0; 1|4|1|2|0|706 × 20 = 14, 1200000,]

Content:
Finally, we add the results:

Content:
[MATH: [math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]; [math]\color{blue}\phantom{0}[/math]|[math]\color{blue}1[/math]; [math]\color{blue}3[/math]; 7|0|6; ×|0|0|0|2|5; 3|5|3|0; +|1|4|1|2|0; 1|7|6|5|0|3, 530 + 14, 120 = 17, 650]

Content:
Therefore, [MATH: 706 \times 25 = 17 , 650.]
